subject: Private deployment boundary & service-mesh handoff — architecture review

From: Eliot Shaw <ops@acme-medical.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: Dana Kim <cloud-partner@orbitalcloud.io>
Date: Thu, 01 Mar 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private deployment architecture review kickoff

Hi Vanessa,

Thanks again for agreeing to run the architecture review for our on-prem setup. We’ve attached the network demarcation doc that our infra team put together and flagged three open questions: control-plane reachability (we prefer customer-hosted control plane but need fallback), TLS mTLS requirements for east-west within our tenant VPC, and how Redwood suggests doing model updates with minimal traffic interruption.

High level constraints: we’re on a colocated site (two racks, dual spine-leaf), upstream BGP to our MPLS, and our security team enforces mTLS between services. We also have an Orbital Cloud SD-WAN appliance for cross-site replication.

Can Redwood provide a short reference architecture (diagram + runbook) showing: control plane placement options (customer vs Redwood-hosted), data-plane egress handoff, and suggested service-mesh/sidecar pattern? We’d like this by EOD Wednesday so we can lock down procurement.

—Eliot
Lead Infrastructure Engineer
Acme Medical Systems

Attachments: acme-net-demarcation.pdf (reference)

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Eliot Shaw <ops@acme-medical.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Dana Kim <cloud-partner@orbitalcloud.io>
Date: Thu, 01 Mar 2028 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment architecture review kickoff

Eliot — thanks for the clear constraints. I attached an initial sketch (2028-03-01-redwood-acme-controlplane-placement-v1.png) that shows three safe patterns:

1) Customer-hosted control plane (preferred for regulated data): Redwood agents run in your tenant VPC; control plane API proxied through mutually authenticated TLS from the management subnet; model artifacts pulled via TLS-backed artifact store.

2) Hybrid control plane: lightweight control-plane components run in-customer (auth, routing), while non-sensitive orchestration (telemetry aggregator, model catalog index) is hosted by Redwood with encrypted telemetry. Fallback routes exist to switch fully to hosted if local infra fails.

3) Fully Redwood-hosted control plane: minimal on-prem footprint (just inference workers) and full routing over a customer-approved VPN/SD-WAN tunnel. Good for teams that want zero ops.

Notes on data plane and service mesh: we recommend a sidecar approach (Envoy) for east-west TLS enforcement with mTLS termination at the sidecar; the inference process communicates to the sidecar on localhost port to avoid exposing application ports. For egress to external APIs or artifact stores, we recommend a dedicated egress proxy in a screened subnet to centralize audit logs and DLP rules.

Open questions for your infra team so we can finalize:
- Can you run a lightweight control-plane VM in the same rack as inference workers? Any co-tenancy constraints?
- Which CA do you prefer for mTLS (internal PKI vs HashiVault-managed certs)?
- Do you need our image signing verification to happen on-prem or can it be validated during pull via signed manifests?

I’ll ask Marcus to detail the network ACLs and port list; Lauren will draft a deployment runbook. If the sketch looks right we’ll iterate and produce a v2 with port-level diagrams.

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Partner Solutions
Redwood Inference

Attachment: 2028-03-01-redwood-acme-controlplane-placement-v1.png

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>

Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Dana Kim <cloud-partner@orbitalcloud.io>

Subject: Re: Private deployment architecture review kickoff

Eliot / team — quick technical follow-up from my side after reviewing the demarcation doc:

- mTLS termination: If Acme requires mTLS between every process, the sidecar model will incur CPU overhead per inference worker. We should size the sidecar for peak qps with TLS offload (Intel QAT or AES-NI) where available.
- Health & KV cache sync: data-plane workers will maintain KV caches for model generation (KV for sessions). We recommend an asynchronous cache-replication channel across the spine for HA; control plane will coordinate invalidation. This avoids synchronous cross-rack calls on the hot path.
- BGP/external handoff: since you have MPLS/BGP upstream, the recommended pattern is to peer egress proxies to the SD-WAN appliance and advertise a /32 for the proxy IPs to avoid leaking internal prefixes.

I attached a second diagram showing the sidecar egress flow and explicit IP ranges to be NATed at the proxy: 2028-03-02-acme-service-mesh-egress-patterns-v2.png. Also suggest a staging run (canary) where we deploy 10% of traffic through the Redwood-hosted model catalog to verify signing/updates before full cutover.

Marcus
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachment: 2028-03-02-acme-service-mesh-egress-patterns-v2.png

Eliot — attached is the draft runbook (runbook-deployment-steps-ACME.md) with step-by-step validation checks for control plane placement, certificate provisioning, and a staged model rollout plan. Highlights:

- Pre-deploy checks: rack-level isolation, CA root import, egress proxy NAT ranges configured.
- Deployment steps: (1) Provision sidecar image with envoy config and certs, (2) Bootstrap control-plane agent on a single node, (3) Canary model fetch & artifact verification, (4) Scale workers and enable traffic splitting.
- Rollback: control-plane agent includes a passive fallback that will re-route to Redwood-hosted model endpoints if artifact verification fails or if the on-prem control plane loses quorum for >2 minutes.

Action items for Acme: confirm CA plan and whether the sidecar can use your Vault for short-lived certs. If confirmed we’ll finalize the diagrams and produce a hardened port ACL table for your firewall team.

Next meeting proposal: Tue Mar 6, 10:00 AM PT — 30 minutes to walk the runbook and sign off.

Thanks,
Vanessa

Attachment: runbook-deployment-steps-ACME.md

Vanessa/Marcus — this looks good and hits all of our hard requirements. A few quick confirmations:

- We will use our internal PKI (HashiCorp Vault) for cert issuance; Vault team is on board to do short-lived certs for sidecars.
- We can host the lightweight control plane VM in Rack 2 (same AZ-equivalent) — capacity confirmed.
- We approve the egress NAT /32 pattern and will coordinate BGP announcements with our network team.

Please push the updated diagrams and the final port ACL table (we need it for our firewall change) and I’ll send an invite for Tue Mar 6 10:00 AM PT. I opened JIRA INF-1423 to track the work.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — looking forward to the runbook walkthrough.

—Eliot
